text:
alert-bot: ALERT: ALB target deregistration spike in prod-edge-eu-west-1 — 4 targets removed in 4m for tg-0a1b2c3d
maria: ugh. noticed latency on webhooks earlier, any idea which nodes?
sam: checking... `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide -l app=edge -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name} {@.status.phase} {@.spec.nodeName}\n{end}'`
sam: output shows several pods moved around: edge-pod-7b9 -> ip-10-0-5-12, edge-pod-3c2 -> ip-10-0-6-45, a bunch with restartCount=1
raj: what time did autoscaler run?
sam: autoscaler events: `ScaleDown: removing 3 nodes (gpu-pool-eu-west1-spot)` at 2026-06-10T03:02:14Z
maria: so scale-down + spot termination -> pods rescheduled -> ALB sees them as unhealthy? but why immediate deregister instead of draining?
elaine: likely: node termination sent SIGTERM, but preStop / terminationGracePeriodSeconds not set, pod process exited quickly and kubelet force-deleted. ALB still had open keepalive sockets to the old backend and got RSTs or timeouts -> target considered unhealthy and removed. Also conntrack entries on nodes got stale during rapid churn.
ops-oncall: we hit this before: short termination window + aggressive scale-down -> LB healthcheck flaps. Quick mitigation: increase TG deregistration delay and healthcheck timeout, and add a preStop sleep to give kube-proxy time to NAT/conntrack drain.
maria: can we roll a hotfix to prod now?
sam: applying annotations to the service targeting the ALB (uses aws-alb-ingress-controller) — patch snippet I used:
```
kubectl annotate service prod-edge svc.kubernetes.io/elb-connection-draining-enabled=true --overwrite
kubectl annotate service prod-edge alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-attributes="deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds=90" --overwrite
```

sam: and bumped health check: `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-timeout-seconds: "8"` and interval -> 10s

raj: also push quick pod change: add preStop hook + terminationGracePeriodSeconds to Deployment so pods sleep 30s on SIGTERM:
```
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 30"]
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40
```

elaine: that helps drain in-flight connections and gives kube-proxy/conntrack time to clear. We should avoid immediate SIGKILL during spot evictions.

ops-oncall: I'll coord with autoscaler settings — we can set the scaleDown unneededTime to 10m for gpu pool so we don't churn during brief dips.
maria: any quick check commands to confirm ALB sees them healthy after changes?

sam: run AWS CLI: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c3d` should show `healthy` states. Also `kubectl get pod -n prod -o wide` to ensure no rapid restarts.

sam: ran describe-target-health -> most targets moved to healthy within 60s after annotation applied.

alert-bot: RESOLVED: ALB target group tg-0a1b2c3d health normalized; 0 deregistrations in last 10m

raj: follow-ups: 1) add preStop + terminationGracePeriod to all edge deployments on gpu pool, 2) change cluster-autoscaler scaleDownUnneededTime for gpu pool to 600s, 3) run a chaos test to simulate spot termination and verify LB behavior, 4) consider increasing conntrack max on nodes if churn expected.

maria: creating a short runbook with commands and the deployment patch, will post in #eng-infra-runbooks and link here. cc @ops-oncall

ops-oncall: noted. rolling patch to other regions after runbook reviews. :thumbsup:

elaine: thanks team — this explains the weird deregistration pattern during the 03:00 scale down window.

sam: leaving the temporary annotations in place for 2h then revert if stable.

maria: 👍
